paragraphs.source_en: I think that for a man like my master, who has soaked in the medicinal bath so long without the slightest effect, the only remedy is to pour vinegar over him and roast him over a fire. Otherwise, even if hundreds of such students appeared and spent decades at it, they would never cure my master’s obstinacy. All these people soaking in the baths and all these people rinsing themselves at the faucets are a band of monsters who have stripped off the clothing indispensable to civilized men; naturally they cannot be judged by ordinary standards, and they may do whatever they please. It would be no great matter if their stomachs marched up to the place of their lungs, if Watonai became a Seiwa Genji, or if Tami-san were distrusted in every possible way. But once a man leaves the washing place and steps up into the dressing room, he is no longer a monster. For he has returned to the world where ordinary human beings live, and must put on the clothing required by civilization. It therefore follows, as a matter of course, that he must conduct himself as a human being does. The place where my master now stands is the threshold: the threshold between the washing place and the dressing room, the crucial moment when he himself is about to return to the genial, smiling, flexible world of social give-and-take. If, even at such a moment, he remains stubborn to the end, then this stubbornness must surely be, for him, an incurable disease. If it is a disease, it cannot be easily rooted out; in my humble opinion, there is only one way to cure it completely, and that is to ask the principal to dismiss him. Once dismissed, a man as inflexible as my master would certainly be left wandering the streets. The final result of wandering the streets would be to die a vagrant’s death. In other words, dismissal would mean death for my master. Though my master enjoys fussing over minor ailments, he is extremely unwilling to die. He merely wants to indulge in the luxury of being a little ill, so long as it does not go so far as death. So if one were to frighten him by saying, “That illness of yours will cost you your life,” timid and cowardly as he is, my master would surely tremble from head to foot. Through that trembling, I imagine, his illness would be rooted out; if even that did not root it out, then there would be no help for him.

units.source_en: I think that for a man like my master, who has soaked in the medicinal bath so long without the slightest effect, the only remedy is to pour vinegar over him and roast him over a fire.
units.source_zh: 我想，像主人这样在药池里浸泡了那么久仍然毫不奏效，就只有浇上醋、用火烤的办法了。

units.source_en: Otherwise, even if hundreds of such students appeared and spent decades at it, they would never cure my master’s obstinacy.
units.source_zh: 否则像这样的“书生”就是来上几百个，用上几十年的工夫，也不会治愈主人的顽固症的。

units.source_en: All these people soaking in the baths and all these people rinsing themselves at the faucets are a band of monsters who have stripped off the clothing indispensable to civilized men; naturally they cannot be judged by ordinary standards, and they may do whatever they please.

ja.t: しにごろごろしているものは

units.source_zh: 这么多在浴池里浸泡着的人，这么多在水龙头前冲澡的人，都是脱掉了文明人所不可缺少的衣服的怪物集团，当然不能用常规来要求他们，他们可以愿意干什么就干什么。

units.source_en: It would be no great matter if their stomachs marched up to the place of their lungs, if Watonai became a Seiwa Genji, or if Tami-san were distrusted in every possible way.
units.source_zh: 他们的胃跑到肺的地方去了，和唐内成了清和源氏，对阿民百般地不信任，这些都未尝不可。

units.source_en: But once a man leaves the washing place and steps up into the dressing room, he is no longer a monster.
units.source_zh: 但是，他一旦从冲澡的地方上到穿衣的厅里来，就不再是怪物。

units.source_en: For he has returned to the world where ordinary human beings live, and must put on the clothing required by civilization.
units.source_zh: 因为他们回到了一般人类所生息的人世，就要穿上文明所必备的衣服。

units.source_en: It therefore follows, as a matter of course, that he must conduct himself as a human being does.

ja.t: をとらなければならんはずである。

units.source_zh: 因而理所当然地必须采取人所采取的行动。

units.source_en: The place where my master now stands is the threshold: the threshold between the washing place and the dressing room, the crucial moment when he himself is about to return to the genial, smiling, flexible world of social give-and-take.
units.source_zh: 现在主人站立的地方是在门槛上，是在介于冲澡地方与穿衣厅的门槛上，是本人即将回到欢言笑语、融通圆滑的世界的关键时刻。

units.source_en: If, even at such a moment, he remains stubborn to the end, then this stubbornness must surely be, for him, an incurable disease.
units.source_zh: 在这样的关键时刻，他还这样顽固到底，可见这种顽固对他本人说来已经是一种不可救药的病症。

units.source_en: If it is a disease, it cannot be easily rooted out; in my humble opinion, there is only one way to cure it completely, and that is to ask the principal to dismiss him. Once dismissed, a man as inflexible as my master would certainly be left wandering the streets.
units.source_zh: 既然是病，那就不是轻易可以根除的，根据在下的卑见，想要根治这种病方法只有一个，那就是去求校长把他革职，一旦革职，像主人那样不会通融的人，肯定要流落街头。

units.source_en: The final result of wandering the streets would be to die a vagrant’s death.

ja.t: にをしなければならない。

units.source_zh: 流落街头的最后结果就是浮浪而死。

units.source_en: In other words, dismissal would mean death for my master.
units.source_zh: 换句话说，革职对主人说来意味着死亡。

units.source_en: Though my master enjoys fussing over minor ailments, he is extremely unwilling to die.
units.source_zh: 主人虽然喜欢闹小病小灾，却是极不愿意死的。

units.source_en: He merely wants to indulge in the luxury of being a little ill, so long as it does not go so far as death.

ja.t: がしていたいのである。

units.source_zh: 他只希望在不至于死的范围内，闹点小病来享受享受。

units.source_en: So if one were to frighten him by saying, “That illness of yours will cost you your life,” timid and cowardly as he is, my master would surely tremble from head to foot.
units.source_zh: 所以如果威吓他说：“你闹这种病会要你命的，”胆小怯懦的主人肯定要吓得浑身发抖。

units.source_en: Through that trembling, I imagine, his illness would be rooted out; if even that did not root it out, then there would be no help for him.

ja.t: ちなければそれまでの

units.source_zh: 通过这种浑身发抖，我想他的病就会根除，如果还是不能根除，那也就无可救药了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 我想，像主人这样在药池里浸泡了那么久仍然毫不奏效，就只有浇上醋、用火烤的办法了。否则像这样的“书生”就是来上几百个，用上几十年的工夫，也不会治愈主人的顽固症的。这么多在浴池里浸泡着的人，这么多在水龙头前冲澡的人，都是脱掉了文明人所不可缺少的衣服的怪物集团，当然不能用常规来要求他们，他们可以愿意干什么就干什么。他们的胃跑到肺的地方去了，和唐内成了清和源氏，对阿民百般地不信任，这些都未尝不可。但是，他一旦从冲澡的地方上到穿衣的厅里来，就不再是怪物。因为他们回到了一般人类所生息的人世，就要穿上文明所必备的衣服。因而理所当然地必须采取人所采取的行动。现在主人站立的地方是在门槛上，是在介于冲澡地方与穿衣厅的门槛上，是本人即将回到欢言笑语、融通圆滑的世界的关键时刻。在这样的关键时刻，他还这样顽固到底，可见这种顽固对他本人说来已经是一种不可救药的病症。既然是病，那就不是轻易可以根除的，根据在下的卑见，想要根治这种病方法只有一个，那就是去求校长把他革职，一旦革职，像主人那样不会通融的人，肯定要流落街头。流落街头的最后结果就是浮浪而死。换句话说，革职对主人说来意味着死亡。主人虽然喜欢闹小病小灾，却是极不愿意死的。他只希望在不至于死的范围内，闹点小病来享受享受。所以如果威吓他说：“你闹这种病会要你命的，”胆小怯懦的主人肯定要吓得浑身发抖。通过这种浑身发抖，我想他的病就会根除，如果还是不能根除，那也就无可救药了。
